CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Bupati is the Bupati of Sanggau.
2. Region is the Regency of Sanggau.
3. Regional Government is the Bupati as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

CHAPTER II
SCOPE OF PROTECTION
Article 2
The scope of Protection of Women from acts of Violence includes: a. prevention;
b. Service/Handling; and
c. empowerment.

Article 20
(1) Regional Government is responsible for implementing efforts for the Protection of Women from acts of Violence in the form of: a. establishing PPT;
b. policy formulation;
c. preparing planning and implementing programs and activities; d. providing support for facilities and infrastructure; and
e. supervising the implementation of services to Victims with minimum service standards.
(2) In carrying out the responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women.
(3) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18
Other violence as referred to in Article 12 letter f includes: a. any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/or
b. a situation where a person/Victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER VI
Article 24
(1) PPT may be established by the Regional Government, vertical agencies in the Region, and/or community institutions.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements from the Regional Police, Regional Apparatus with authority over Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions, which function to provide protection to women from acts of Violence carried out in a networked manner.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to provide services and temporary protection in the form of Safe Houses (shelters) for Victims.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have a Safe House as referred to in paragraph (3), then the Victim shall be referred to a PPT that has a Safe House.
(5) Provisions regarding the establishment, composition of the management team and organizational structure of PPT established by the Regional Government shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

What is meant by efforts from the preventive aspect is efforts that prioritize the prevention aspect with targets being communities that are vulnerable to being affected by/becoming Victims of Violence and experiencing its impact. Preventive efforts can be carried out through community empowerment in the form of training activities and others.
What is meant by efforts from the curative aspect is efforts carried out in the form of handling for Victims of Violence who require handling according to their needs, namely health rehabilitation handling if the Victim suffers the impact of Violence physically or psychologically, provision of Assistance and Law Enforcement for Victims who require Assistance and Law Enforcement, and so forth.
What is meant by the rehabilitative aspect is efforts carried out as an effort to recover Victims of Violence both physically, psychologically and psychosocially.

NUMBER 12 OF 2019
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

THE REGENT OF SANGGAU,

Article 17
Exploitation as referred to in Article 12 letter e includes:
a. actions that exploit women economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. actions with or without the consent of the Victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.

Article 23
(1) Efforts to provide and organize Services/Handling for Victims are carried out in a networked manner.
(2) The network as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to: a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of PPT services;
b. develop networks and referral systems; and
c. collect, compile and present reports on Violence. (3) The network as referred to in paragraph (2) carries out its duties and functions in accordance with the form of services as referred to in Article 6.

Article 13
Physical violence as referred to in Article 12 letter a includes acts that result in pain, wounds, injury or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting, and/or death.

Article 19
Letter a What is meant by "the right to have one's dignity respected as a human being" is upholding human rights.
Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain explanations, questions, ideas, and signs containing value, meaning and messages whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of Violence.
Letter e Sufficiently clear.
Letter f What is meant by "the right to obtain compensation" includes: economic empowerment, return costs, health and education or skills guarantees.
Letter g What is meant by "the right to obtain Social Rehabilitation" includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, Legal Aid to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship.
Letter h What is meant by "the right to obtain Complaint Handling" is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.
Letter i Sufficiently clear.
Letter j What is meant by "the right to obtain Assistance" includes among others: psychologists, psychiatrists and health experts, religious counselors, advocates and Family members.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 28
(1) Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women's Protection.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers planning and implementation.
(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers planning, implementation, governance, financing, quality, control, and supervision.
(5) Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(6) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted based on laws and regulations periodically every 6 (six) months.

Article 16
Neglect as referred to in Article 12 letter d includes:
a. acts that neglect women within the scope of their household; and/or
b. acts that result in economic dependence.

Article 4
In addition to prevention efforts carried out by the Regional Government as referred to in Article 3, prevention efforts are also carried out by the Family and/or closest relatives, community, educational institutions and customary institutions.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

Article 17
Exploitation as referred to in Article 12 letter e includes:
a. actions that exploit women economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Article 20
(1) Regional Government is responsible for implementing efforts for the Protection of Women from acts of Violence in the form of: a. establishing PPT;

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.

11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.

Article 24

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Bupati is the Bupati of Sanggau.
2. Region is the Regency of Sanggau.
3. Regional Government is the Bupati as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Bupati is the Bupati of Sanggau.
2. Region is the Regency of Sanggau.
3. Regional Government is the Bupati as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Bupati is the Bupati of Sanggau.
2. Region is the Regency of Sanggau.
3. Regional Government is the Bupati as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

Article 16

a. acts that neglect women within the scope of their household; and/or
b. acts that result in economic dependence.

4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

SCOPE OF PROTECTION
Article 2
The scope of Protection of Women from acts of Violence includes: a. prevention;
b. Service/Handling; and
c. empowerment.

Article 20
(1) Regional Government is responsible for implementing efforts for the Protection of Women from acts of Violence in the form of: a. establishing PPT;
b. policy formulation;
c. preparing planning and implementing programs and activities; d. providing support for facilities and infrastructure; and
e. supervising the implementation of services to Victims with minimum service standards.
(2) In carrying out the responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women.

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

CHAPTER VI
Article 24
(1) PPT may be established by the Regional Government, vertical agencies in the Region, and/or community institutions.

6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.

Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

b. actions with or without the consent of the Victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

b. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Bupati is the Bupati of Sanggau.
2. Region is the Regency of Sanggau.
3. Regional Government is the Bupati as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

e. supervising the implementation of services to Victims with minimum service standards.

In addition to prevention efforts carried out by the Regional Government as referred to in Article 3, prevention efforts are also carried out by the Family and/or closest relatives, community, educational institutions and customary institutions.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

REGENT OF SANGGAU

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Bupati is the Bupati of Sanggau.
2. Region is the Regency of Sanggau.
3. Regional Government is the Bupati as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

Article 20
(1) Regional Government is responsible for implementing efforts for the Protection of Women from acts of Violence in the form of: a. establishing PPT;
b. policy formulation;
c. preparing planning and implementing programs and activities; d. providing support for facilities and infrastructure; and
e. supervising the implementation of services to Victims with minimum service standards.
(2) In carrying out the responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women.
(3) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

CHAPTER VI
Article 24
(1) PPT may be established by the Regional Government, vertical agencies in the Region, and/or community institutions.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements from the Regional Police, Regional Apparatus with authority over Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions, which function to provide protection to women from acts of Violence carried out in a networked manner.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to provide services and temporary protection in the form of Safe Houses (shelters) for Victims.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have a Safe House as referred to in paragraph (3), then the Victim shall be referred to a PPT that has a Safe House.
(5) Provisions regarding the establishment, composition of the management team and organizational structure of PPT established by the Regional Government shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

Article 20
(1) Regional Government is responsible for implementing efforts for the Protection of Women from acts of Violence in the form of: a. establishing PPT;
b. policy formulation;
c. preparing planning and implementing programs and activities; d. providing support for facilities and infrastructure; and
e. supervising the implementation of services to Victims with minimum service standards.
(2) In carrying out the responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women.
(3) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI
Article 24
(1) PPT may be established by the Regional Government, vertical agencies in the Region, and/or community institutions.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements from the Regional Police, Regional Apparatus with authority over Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions, which function to provide protection to women from acts of Violence carried out in a networked manner.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to provide services and temporary protection in the form of Safe Houses (shelters) for Victims.

(5) Provisions regarding the establishment, composition of the management team and organizational structure of PPT established by the Regional Government shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.

12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.

16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.

Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Bupati is the Bupati of Sanggau.
2. Region is the Regency of Sanggau.
3. Regional Government is the Bupati as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Bupati and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the Victim.
6. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.

I. GENERAL
Acts of Violence Against Women constitute a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and ordained role, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome Violence Against Women in Sanggau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women.
Protection of Women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the Protection of Women Victims of Violence have not yet regulated efforts for the Protection of Women at the regional level, therefore institutional and regulatory support at the regional level is needed to ensure its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the Protection of Women specifically in the form of prevention, Services/Handling, and empowerment of women in Sanggau Regency.

CHAPTER VI
Article 24
(1) PPT may be established by the Regional Government, vertical agencies in the Region, and/or community institutions.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements from the Regional Police, Regional Apparatus with authority over Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions, which function to provide protection to women from acts of Violence carried out in a networked manner.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to provide services and temporary protection in the form of Safe Houses (shelters) for Victims.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have a Safe House as referred to in paragraph (3), then the Victim shall be referred to a PPT that has a Safe House.
(5) Provisions regarding the establishment, composition of the management team and organizational structure of PPT established by the Regional Government shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

Article 17
Exploitation as referred to in Article 12 letter e includes:
a. actions that exploit women economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. actions with or without the consent of the Victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

7. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence and life vulnerability.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that Violence Against Women will, is, or has occurred.
9. Service/Handling is action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that Violence against the Victim will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
10. Assistance is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for Victims of Violence.
12. Safe House is a residence for Victims during the Assistance process for the security and comfort of Victims from threats and danger.
13. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence Against Women submitted by Victims, Family and community.
14. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
15. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
16. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of Assistance to witnesses and/or Victims of Violence Against Women that is gender sensitive.
17. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return women Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with Family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for Victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward.
